title: Indian frigate joins US, Japanese and Australian navies for Malabar exercise off Japan
dek: INS Sahyadri reached Yokosuka for the four-nation Malabar 2026 drills, which bring together the navies of the Quad countries.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
The Indian Navy's stealth frigate INS Sahyadri has arrived at the Yokosuka naval base in Japan to take part in Malabar 2026, the annual exercise of the navies of India, Japan, the United States and Australia, the four members of the Quad.

The ship, part of the Navy's Eastern Fleet, reached Yokosuka on Wednesday, one report said, citing the Ministry of Defence. The exercise has a harbour phase of planning and professional exchanges, followed by a sea phase in which Sahyadri will operate alongside US, Australian and Japanese units. The ministry said the aim was to build trust and maritime cooperation among the four countries and to contribute to a "secure and stable Indo-Pacific region".

According to another report, citing a Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force release, the drills run from 5 to 12 November south of Japan's Kanto region and include anti-submarine and anti-surface warfare. Australia is sending the frigate HMAS Stuart and a P-8A Poseidon patrol aircraft.

Malabar began as an India-US exercise in 1992 and has included all four Quad navies since 2020. Last year's edition was held off Guam. This year's drills come as the Quad partners step up maritime cooperation across the Indo-Pacific. India's Defence Ministry linked Sahyadri's participation to its MAHASAGAR policy for maritime security and growth in the region.
